questions.prompt: A response from app.example.com sets a cookie without a Domain attribute. Which host scope is established?

choices.text: A domain cookie shared automatically with every example.com subdomain.
A host-only cookie for app.example.com.
A cookie scoped to whichever parent domain is named in the current page URL path.
A cookie shared with sibling hosts whenever its Path is set to slash.

questions.explanation: Without Domain, the cookie is host-only. Parent and sibling hosts do not receive it just because they share a suffix.

questions.prompt: A server wants to expire a stored cookie. Why must its deletion response match the original Domain and Path?

choices.text: Those attributes participate in identifying which stored cookie is replaced.
Only the cookie name identifies replacement, so domain and path need not match.
Matching Path deletes every same-name cookie regardless of the original domain.
Matching Domain deletes every same-name cookie regardless of the original path.

questions.explanation: Cookie replacement identity includes name, domain and path. Expiring a different scoped cookie does not necessarily remove the original.

questions.prompt: A session cookie has HttpOnly but no Secure flag. Which protection does HttpOnly provide?

choices.text: It guarantees that the cookie is sent only through secure transport channels.
It prevents the cookie from accompanying requests initiated by JavaScript.
It makes the cookie accessible to script only while a fetch request is running.
It excludes the cookie from non-HTTP script APIs, not from all insecure transport.

questions.explanation: HttpOnly restricts non-HTTP access such as document.cookie. Secure is the transport flag; HttpOnly does not prevent sending the cookie on applicable requests.

questions.prompt: A same-origin fetch should avoid sending cookies. Which credentials setting expresses that request?

choices.text: same-origin excludes cookies even when the target origin matches the page.
include excludes cookies from requests but accepts them from responses only.
omit excludes credentials from the fetch request.
no-cors excludes credentials independently of the fetch credentials setting.

questions.explanation: Omit excludes credentials. Include requests inclusion, and same-origin permits credentials on same-origin requests. Mode and credentials are separate settings.

questions.prompt: app.example.com tries to set Domain=unrelated.test. How should a conforming user agent treat that domain scope?

choices.text: Accept the scope because an explicit Domain overrides the setting host restriction.
Reject the cookie because the domain does not match the setting host.
Accept the scope when Secure is present because HTTPS authorizes any cookie domain.
Accept the scope when Path is slash because root cookies are cross-domain.

questions.explanation: A server cannot set an arbitrary unrelated cookie domain. Domain matching restricts accepted scope.

questions.prompt: A cookie has Path=/account. Which request path normally path-matches?

choices.text: /account/settings matches the account path scope.
/accounting matches because it begins with the same string without a slash boundary.
/public/account matches because the scoped directory occurs anywhere in the path.
/Account matches because cookie path comparisons are case-insensitive.

questions.explanation: A cookie path matches identical paths or appropriate slash-separated prefixes. /accounting is not a directory-prefix match for /account.

questions.prompt: A team scopes session cookies. Which domain rules hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: An accepted Domain can include matching subdomains.
A Secure cookie may use any unrelated Domain because TLS grants domain authority.
Path automatically grants access to unrelated domains.
Every omitted Domain defaults to the top-level domain.
Omitting Domain creates a host-only cookie.

questions.explanation: a: Domain cookies are sent to domain-matching hosts. b: Secure transport does not waive the cookie domain-match requirement. c: Path matching does not override host or domain scope. d: The default is host-only, not broad top-level scope. e: It is restricted to the setting host.

questions.prompt: A service maintains several scoped cookies. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Path=/account normally matches /account/settings.
Path=/account must also match /accounting.
Path is a reliable security isolation boundary against same-host scripts.
Name, domain and path identify replacement scope.
Deleting a cookie requires targeting its original scope.

questions.explanation: a: The following slash satisfies path matching. b: That prefix lacks the required slash boundary. c: The cookie standard cautions that Path is not a security boundary. d: A new cookie with matching identity replaces the prior one. e: Expiry on a differently scoped cookie may leave the original.

questions.prompt: A session cookie uses Secure and HttpOnly. Which claims hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: HttpOnly alone guarantees secure transport.
Secure prevents every malicious same-origin script action.
Secure restricts sending to secure transport.
HttpOnly restricts non-HTTP script access.
HttpOnly cookies cannot accompany HTTP requests initiated through fetch.

questions.explanation: a: That is the separate purpose of Secure. b: Transport scope is not a complete script security defense. c: It is the transport-related cookie attribute. d: It keeps the cookie outside APIs such as document.cookie. e: HttpOnly restricts non-HTTP script APIs, not applicable HTTP request attachment.

questions.prompt: A developer combines cookies and fetch. Which behaviors hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: no-cors makes Set-Cookie directly readable by JavaScript.
omit excludes credentials for the request.
same-origin permits credentials for a matching origin.
Set-Cookie is not exposed as an ordinary readable response header.
include guarantees every stored cookie is sent to every destination.

questions.explanation: a: No-cors does not expose forbidden headers or opaque response details. b: That is the fetch credentials-mode contract. c: It limits their inclusion to same-origin requests. d: Fetch filters that forbidden response-header name. e: Cookie scope and other cookie restrictions still apply.
